Table 1 row 10 ('valiant_gadget_double_minor_one') states the symbolic 0/2-coupling expansion equals 2(P_0 + w_1 w_2 P_12) without explicitly showing in the paper whether row n+1 of the full (n+3)x(n+3) matrix E (including edge n+1 -> c_1) is scaled by 2 to clear the 1/2 denominator consistently across both S=empty and S={e1, e2}.

Theorem 2.3(2) / Table 1 rows 16-18: Lean Theorems 16-18 formalize simplified integer/list inequalities (List Int additivity, W>=0 & P>M+W, and 2^{m^2} > (2^m)^k for m >= k+1) rather than Strassen tensor prices with log factors or the full exp(c (log N)^2 / (log log N)^2) bound; the prose in Theorem 2.3(2) does transparently note the omission of the (log log N)^2 divisor.

summary: The manuscript formalizes and certifies finite-order algebraic components of OpenAI's November 2026 permanent/Hamiltonian circuit lower-bound framework [3] via an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (v4.35.0, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) and a pure-stdlib zero-float exact-Q Python verifier (PERM-HAM-CERT-1.0). The three main theorem groups cover (i) characteristic-2 Per/det collapse vs. HC non-collapse, (ii) exact 0/2-coupling soundness and char-2 obstruction of the 3x3 Valiant gadget A_Val, and (iii) Ryser inclusion-exclusion, exact Cayley-orthogonal Boson-Sampling amplitudes, and elementary integer/list abstractions of wire-price and superpolynomial degree dominance. All mathematical identities, sparse degree-3 circulant values (N=3..10), scaling curves, and cross-table figures visible in the PDF are exact and internally consistent, and Section 5 honestly delineates the finite-order scope relative to [3]'s full asymptotic machinery. Only minor exposition and proof-detail issues are present, with no unresolved material objections.
weaknesses: Lean 4 formalization covers only small finite matrix orders (n=2,3,4 for Per/det/HC and Ryser) and simplified integer/list inequalities (Theorems 16-18) rather than general-n proofs or the asymptotic CAT(0)/border-complexity engine of [3].

Theorem 2.3(1) omits inline proofs for general-n Ryser inclusion-exclusion, Cayley orthogonality Q^T Q = I_m, and collision-free probability bound Per(Q_sub)^2 <= 1, and does not formally define Q_sub's distinct-row/column selection condition in the theorem text.

All 16 certificates, Lean source code, and the 54 adversarial test suite reside in an external repository and cannot be independently inspected or executed from the PDF alone; similarly, Mode 1 coupled-matrix entries (Table 2) are not listed in the PDF.

Theorem 2.2(2) implicitly assumes the deleted edges e1, e2 have weights w1, w2 matching the entries of B being replaced and states 'vertex-disjoint' (row- and column-disjoint suffices for permanents).
